# The chimera command line

<!-- Generated by python tools/gen_cli_docs.py --lang en. Do not edit by hand: change modules/cli/registry.py and modules/locales/en.json. -->

Everything you can do in the Chimera interface, you can do with the `chimera …` command. Help is built in: `chimera --help`, `chimera <command> --help`, `chimera docs`.

Run without arguments from a terminal, it prints the help; double-clicking `Chimera.exe` opens the window. `chimera --window` and `chimera --browser` open the window or a browser tab.

## Common parameters

- `--json` — machine-readable output
- `--show-secrets` — do not hide secrets
- `--lang` — output language: ru or en (by default from the settings)
- `-h/--help` — help
- `--version` — version

## Exit codes

- `0` — success
- `1` — execution error (the app refused, no such object, network failure)
- `2` — invalid arguments
- `3` — Chimera is not running, the app is too old, or there is no connection

## The `--json` format

The output is a single object:

- `schema` — output format version (currently 1); it grows only on incompatible changes
- `ok` — true/false: whether the command succeeded
- `command` — the command without parameters, for example `winws start`
- `level` — read | app | system: what the command changes (only when ok=true)
- `data` — what the app method returned, losslessly; for composite commands (status, check) a summary
- `error` — when ok=false: {code, message, key, params}; code is usage, not_running, app_too_old, remote_error, forbidden, …; key and params are the message key in the catalog and its parameters (not every error has them); message depends on the language, code and key do not

## Command levels

- `read` — read-only
- `app` — changes the app
- `system` — changes the system

Levels exist so that remote channels can be restricted. The proxy link is hidden in the output; `--show-secrets` shows it. The Telegram proxy link and secret are always shown: they are the key to your own local proxy.

Not turned into commands (with reasons):

- `dispatch` — internal entry point of the window bridge; the control channel has its own
- `shutdown` — stops the modules when the window closes; in a terminal that is `chimera stop`
- `app_elevate` — UAC belongs to the local window; run commands from a terminal with the required privileges.
- `open_url` — opens a link in the browser on the user's computer; in a terminal the address is already visible
- `tg_open_link` — opens Telegram on this computer; `chimera tg link` gives you the link
- `hub_snapshot` — the window's subscription to state push events
- `hub_watch` — the window's subscription to state push events
- `hub_refresh` — the window's subscription to state push events
- `block_check_start` — results arrive as push events in the window; in the CLI `chimera check list <list>` does the same
- `chebur_check_start` — results arrive as push events in the window; in the CLI `chimera check list <list>` does the same

## Commands in detail

### status

What is running right now.

#### `chimera status`

State of the app and its modules: bypass, proxy, Telegram proxy, hosts. Level: read-only.

```
chimera status
chimera status --json
```

### start

Start Chimera without a window (in the tray).

#### `chimera start`

Start Chimera without a window, in the tray. The program itself asks for administrator rights. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera start
```

### tui

Keyboard terminal menu (arrows/WASD, live state)..

#### `chimera tui [--simple]`

Keyboard terminal interface: Overview, Strategies, Lists, Proxy, Hosts, DNS, Telegram, Logs, Settings. Arrows/WASD select a row, Enter/D performs an action, Esc/A returns to the menu. Numbers 1–9 select an item in the current menu; Ctrl+1–9 opens a section. E in Lists opens the terminal editor: Ctrl+S saves, Esc keeps a draft. Ctrl+E explains a site route. Mouse is disabled. Connects to Chimera (starts it without a window if needed); quitting (q) keeps Chimera running. Falls back to a simple menu without a terminal or Textual. --simple uses a numbered menu with its own Api. A colon opens a command prompt with history and results. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

- `--simple` — simple numbered menu instead of the full-screen interface

```
chimera tui
chimera tui --simple
```

### stop

Close Chimera.

#### `chimera stop`

Close Chimera and shut its modules down. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera stop
```

### restart

Restart Chimera.

#### `chimera restart`

Restart Chimera. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera restart
```

### version

Program and protocol version.

#### `chimera version`

Program version and command-line protocol version. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

```
chimera --version
chimera version --json
```

### update

Update Chimera.

#### `chimera update state`

Update state: current and found versions, stage. Level: read-only.

```
chimera update state
```

#### `chimera update check`

Check whether a new version is out. Level: read-only.

```
chimera update check
```

#### `chimera update install`

Download, verify and install the version that was found; the program restarts. Level: changes the system.

```
chimera update check && chimera update install
```

### autostart

Start Chimera with Windows.

#### `chimera autostart state`

Whether Chimera starts with Windows. Level: read-only.

```
chimera autostart state
```

#### `chimera autostart set <on|off>`

Turn starting with Windows on or off (needs administrator rights). Level: changes the system.

- `value` — on or off

```
chimera autostart set on
```

### discord

Clear the Discord cache.

#### `chimera discord clear-cache`

Clear the Discord cache (Discord must be closed). Level: changes the app.

```
chimera discord clear-cache
```

### sources

External sources: zapret2, Flowseal strategies and others.

#### `chimera sources versions`

Local versions of the external sources (no network). Level: read-only.

```
chimera sources versions
```

#### `chimera sources check [name]`

Compare source versions with GitHub (all of them or one). Level: read-only.

- `name` — source; without a name, all of them

```
chimera sources check
chimera sources check zapret2
```

#### `chimera sources update <name>`

Pull the latest version of a source (git fetch + checkout). Level: changes the system.

- `name` — source from `chimera sources versions`

```
chimera sources update zapret2
```

### config

Program settings (config.json).

#### `chimera config get [key]`

Show the program settings: all of them or one. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `key` — setting name; without it, all of them

```
chimera config get
chimera config get update_channel
```

#### `chimera config set <key> <value>`

Change a setting. Available are the ones the window changes: ui_backend, auto_elevate, close_to_tray, update_channel, update_check, theme (system, light or dark), lang (auto, ru or en). Anything else means editing config.json by hand. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

- `key` — setting name
- `value` — true/false, a number or a string

```
chimera config set update_channel beta
chimera config set close_to_tray false
chimera config set theme dark
```

#### `chimera config export [--sections <sections>] [--file <file>]`

Build a config to send: sections from --sections (by default the portable ones: lists,proxy,hosts,dns,telegram; winws depends on the provider and is included only explicitly). The proxy link and secrets are not included. --file writes it to a file. Level: read-only.

- `--sections` — sections, comma-separated
- `--file` — write to a file

```
chimera config export --file my.chimera
chimera config export --sections proxy,lists
```

#### `chimera config import-preview <file>`

Show what someone else's config would change (a file, or `-` for stdin): what would be applied, what skipped, what needs confirmation. Changes nothing. Level: read-only.

- `file` — config file, or - for stdin

```
chimera config import-preview friend.chimera
```

#### `chimera config import <file> [--sections <sections>] [--confirm]`

Apply someone else's config (sections from --sections, by default all except the provider-dependent ones). Look at `config import-preview` first. Foreign DNS/hosts servers and Telegram domains only with --confirm. The files are copied to data/backups before anything is applied. Level: changes the app.

- `file` — config file, or - for stdin
- `--sections` — sections, comma-separated
- `--confirm` — allow foreign DNS/hosts servers and Telegram domains

```
chimera config import friend.chimera --sections proxy,lists
```

#### `chimera config appearance`

Current appearance. Level: read-only.

```
chimera config appearance --json
```

#### `chimera config appearance-preview <settings>`

Preview appearance without saving. Level: read-only.

- `settings` — JSON: theme and appearance.

```
chimera config appearance-preview '{"theme":"dark","appearance":{"palette":"dracula"}}' --json
```

#### `chimera config appearance-apply <settings>`

Apply appearance with a configuration snapshot. Level: changes the app.

- `settings` — JSON: theme and appearance.

```
chimera config appearance-apply '{"appearance":{"radius":"rounded"}}'
```

#### `chimera config appearance-refresh`

Refresh the theme catalog from GitHub. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera config appearance-refresh
```

#### `chimera config backup`

Create a manual snapshot of all Chimera settings and user lists. Does not change running modules. Local snapshots contain secrets; output only shows the snapshot name and sections. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera config backup
chimera config backup --json
```

#### `chimera config verify <domains…>`

Check sites and save a full verified snapshot Level: changes the app.

- `domains` — 1 to 6 comma-separated domains; every site must respond successfully

```
chimera config verify youtube.com,discord.com
```

#### `chimera config verified`

Show the last verified snapshot and its sites Level: read-only.

```
chimera config verified --json
```

#### `chimera config backups`

List local configuration snapshots, including pre-import snapshots. Secret values are hidden. Level: read-only.

```
chimera config backups
chimera config backups --json
```

#### `chimera config compare <first> <second>`

Compare two saved snapshots without applying settings. Level: read-only.

- `first` — First snapshot ID (original state).
- `second` — Second snapshot ID (changed state).

```
chimera config compare 20260930-120000-001-manual 20260930-130000-001-manual --json
```

#### `chimera config restore-preview <id>`

Validate a snapshot and preview settings and lists to restore. Changes nothing; secrets stay hidden. Level: read-only.

- `id` — snapshot directory name from config backups, without a path

```
chimera config restore-preview 20260930-120000-001-import
```

#### `chimera config restore <id> [--confirm]`

Restore a local snapshot with --confirm. Current settings are saved first, then applied to running modules; failures trigger rollback. Previously stopped modules stay stopped. Level: changes the system.

- `id` — snapshot directory name from config backups, without a path
- `--confirm` — confirm replacing settings and applying them to running modules

```
chimera config restore 20260930-120000-001-import --confirm
```

### lang

Program language.

#### `chimera lang show`

Program language: what is chosen in the settings, what is in effect now and what the system uses. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

```
chimera lang show
chimera lang show --json
```

#### `chimera lang set <auto|ru|en>`

Choose the program language: auto (as in Windows), ru or en. The `--lang` flag and the CHIMERA_LANG variable take priority. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

- `value` — auto, ru or en

```
chimera lang set en
chimera lang set auto
```

#### `chimera lang catalog [ru|en]`

The whole text catalog of a language (for the window and for checks): key → text. Without a language, the current one. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `language` — ru or en; without it, the current one

```
chimera lang catalog en --json
```

### winws

DPI bypass (zapret2 / winws2).

#### `chimera winws state`

Bypass state: running or not, strategy, lists, error, version. Level: read-only.

```
chimera winws state
```

#### `chimera winws strategies`

List of available strategies. Level: read-only.

```
chimera winws strategies --json
```

#### `chimera winws start [strategy]`

Start a strategy. Without a name, the last one used. Level: changes the system.

- `strategy` — id from `chimera winws strategies`; the last one by default

```
chimera winws start
chimera winws start alt2
```

#### `chimera winws stop`

Stop the bypass. Level: changes the system.

```
chimera winws stop
```

#### `chimera winws autostart <on|off>`

Start the strategy when Chimera starts. Level: changes the app.

- `value` — on or off

```
chimera winws autostart on
```

#### `chimera winws lists [lists…]`

Which domain lists to send through the bypass (no names clears them). Applied right away. Level: changes the app.

- `lists` — list names

```
chimera winws lists youtube discord
```

#### `chimera winws filters`

Filter state: game, ipset, fake blobs. Level: read-only.

```
chimera winws filters
```

#### `chimera winws game <off|all|tcp|udp> [--tcp <tcp>] [--udp <udp>]`

Game filter: off, all, tcp or udp; ports are optional. Level: changes the system.

- `mode` — mode
- `--tcp` — TCP port range
- `--udp` — UDP port range

```
chimera winws game udp
chimera winws game all --tcp 1024-65535
```

#### `chimera winws ipset <none|any|loaded>`

ipset mode: none, any or loaded. Level: changes the app.

- `mode` — mode

```
chimera winws ipset loaded
```

#### `chimera winws ipset-update`

Download a fresh subnet list (ipset). Level: changes the system.

```
chimera winws ipset-update
```

#### `chimera winws fake <slot> <blob>`

Put a fake blob into a slot (discord or game). Level: changes the app.

- `slot` — slot from `chimera winws filters`
- `blob` — blob name

```
chimera winws fake discord quic_initial_www_google_com
```

### proxy

Sing-box proxy.

#### `chimera proxy state`

Proxy state: running or not, mode, lists, domain count, core. Level: read-only.

```
chimera proxy state
```

#### `chimera proxy start`

Start the proxy (sing-box). Level: changes the system.

```
chimera proxy start
```

#### `chimera proxy stop`

Stop the proxy. Level: changes the system.

```
chimera proxy stop
```

#### `chimera proxy mode <pac|split|tun>`

Proxy mode: pac (no admin needed), split (selective TUN) or tun (all traffic). Level: changes the system.

- `mode` — mode

```
chimera proxy mode pac
```

#### `chimera proxy link [link] [--clear]`

Set the proxy link (vless://, trojan://, ss://, vmess://). `-` reads it from stdin, `--clear` removes it. Level: changes the app.

- `link` — link, or `-`
- `--clear` — remove the link

```
chimera proxy link vless://...
echo vless://... | chimera proxy link -
chimera proxy link --clear
```

#### `chimera proxy lists [lists…]`

Which lists go through the proxy (no names clears them). Applied right away. Level: changes the app.

- `lists` — list names

```
chimera proxy lists youtube telegram
```

#### `chimera proxy apps [apps…]`

Apps for selective TUN, by executable name (Discord.exe). No names clears them. Level: changes the app.

- `apps` — Discord.exe …

```
chimera proxy apps Discord.exe chrome.exe
```

#### `chimera proxy apps-running`

Programs the user is running right now (for picking them for selective TUN). Level: read-only.

```
chimera proxy apps-running
```

#### `chimera proxy autostart <on|off>`

Start the proxy when Chimera starts. Level: changes the app.

- `value` — on or off

```
chimera proxy autostart on
```

#### `chimera proxy core-download`

Download the sing-box core (pinned version, SHA256 verified). Level: changes the app.

```
chimera proxy core-download
```

### tg

Telegram proxy.

#### `chimera tg state`

State of the Telegram proxy and its settings. Level: read-only.

```
chimera tg state
```

#### `chimera tg start`

Start the Telegram proxy. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera tg start
```

#### `chimera tg stop`

Stop the Telegram proxy. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera tg stop
```

#### `chimera tg stats`

Counters of the running Telegram proxy. Level: read-only.

```
chimera tg stats
```

#### `chimera tg link`

The tg://proxy link to connect Telegram. Level: read-only.

```
chimera tg link
```

#### `chimera tg config [--host <host>] [--port <port>] [--secret <secret>] [--autostart <autostart>]`

Change the address, port, secret or autostart (everything else stays as is). Level: changes the app.

- `--host` — address; 0.0.0.0 opens it to devices on the network
- `--port` — port
- `--secret` — secret of 32 hex characters
- `--autostart` — on or off

```
chimera tg config --port 1443
chimera tg config --host 0.0.0.0
```

#### `chimera tg regen-secret`

Generate a new secret (the old link stops working). Level: changes the app.

```
chimera tg regen-secret
```

#### `chimera tg advanced <settings…>`

Advanced core settings: key=value (the value is JSON or a string). Level: changes the app.

- `settings` — key=value …

```
chimera tg advanced fake_tls_domain=example.com
chimera tg advanced fallback_cfproxy=false
```

#### `chimera tg check-update`

Check for an update of the Telegram proxy core. Level: read-only.

```
chimera tg check-update
```

### hosts

IP substitution in the system hosts file.

#### `chimera hosts state`

State of the hosts substitution: applied or not, how many entries. Level: read-only.

```
chimera hosts state
```

#### `chimera hosts overview`

Everything about hosts: providers, lists, bindings, state. Level: read-only.

```
chimera hosts overview --json
```

#### `chimera hosts on`

Turn the hosts substitution on (bindings are kept). Level: changes the system.

```
chimera hosts on
```

#### `chimera hosts off`

Turn the hosts substitution off: the block is removed from the file, bindings stay. Level: changes the system.

```
chimera hosts off
```

#### `chimera hosts assign [bindings…] [--replace]`

Bind lists to providers: provider=list,list (empty unbinds). Only the providers you name change; --replace replaces all bindings. Level: changes the system.

- `bindings` — provider=list,list …
- `--replace` — replace all bindings

```
chimera hosts assign comss=youtube,discord
chimera hosts assign xbox=
```

#### `chimera hosts provider-add <name> <doh> <servers…>`

Add a hosts provider (name, DoH address, servers). Level: changes the app.

- `name` — str
- `doh` — DoH address, or -
- `servers` — IP addresses

```
chimera hosts provider-add my https://dns.example/dns-query 1.2.3.4
```

#### `chimera hosts provider-delete <id>`

Delete a hosts provider. Level: changes the app.

- `id` — provider id

```
chimera hosts provider-delete my
```

#### `chimera hosts ping <id>`

Check that a hosts provider is reachable. Level: read-only.

- `id` — provider id

```
chimera hosts ping comss
```

#### `chimera hosts background [settings…]`

Hosts background settings: key=value (JSON values). refresh_interval and check_interval are positive integer seconds; refresh_enabled/check_enabled/autoswitch_enabled are true/false; provider_order is an array of IDs. Level: changes the app.

- `settings` — key=value …

```
chimera hosts background
chimera hosts background refresh_enabled=true refresh_interval=21600
chimera hosts background check_enabled=true check_interval=900
```

### dns

System DNS and DNS providers.

#### `chimera dns state`

Adapters, their current DNS and providers. Level: read-only.

```
chimera dns state
```

#### `chimera dns ping [id]`

Ping DNS providers: all of them or one. Level: read-only.

- `id` — provider; without it, all of them

```
chimera dns ping
```

#### `chimera dns probe <id>`

Check whether a provider answers for “bypass” and ad domains. Level: read-only.

- `id` — provider id

```
chimera dns probe cloudflare
```

#### `chimera dns probe-config [--bypass <bypass>] [--ad <ad>]`

Probe domains: show them, or set --bypass and --ad. Level: changes the app.

- `--bypass` — domain for the “bypass” probe
- `--ad` — domain for the ad probe

```
chimera dns probe-config
chimera dns probe-config --bypass rutracker.org
```

#### `chimera dns set <adapter> <provider>`

Set a DNS provider on an adapter (needs administrator rights). Level: changes the system.

- `adapter` — adapter number from `chimera dns state`
- `provider` — provider id

```
chimera dns set 12 cloudflare
```

#### `chimera dns reset <adapter>`

Return an adapter's DNS to automatic (DHCP). Level: changes the system.

- `adapter` — adapter number from `chimera dns state`

```
chimera dns reset 12
```

#### `chimera dns provider-add <name> <servers…> [--ipv6 <ipv6>] [--doh <doh>] [--dot <dot>] [--unblock] [--filtering]`

Add a DNS provider. Level: changes the app.

- `name` — str
- `servers` — IPv4 addresses
- `--ipv6` — IPv6 addresses, comma-separated
- `--doh` — DoH address
- `--dot` — DoT name
- `--unblock` — unblocking
- `--filtering` — with filtering

```
chimera dns provider-add my 9.9.9.9 149.112.112.112 --doh https://dns.quad9.net/dns-query
```

#### `chimera dns provider-delete <id>`

Delete a DNS provider. Level: changes the app.

- `id` — provider id

```
chimera dns provider-delete my
```

#### `chimera dns provider-edit <id> <name> <servers…> [--ipv6 <ipv6>] [--doh <doh>] [--dot <dot>] [--unblock] [--filtering]`

Edit your DNS provider: the name and addresses are set again in full. Level: changes the app.

- `id` — provider id
- `name` — str
- `servers` — IPv4 addresses
- `--ipv6` — IPv6 addresses, comma-separated
- `--doh` — DoH address
- `--dot` — DoT name
- `--unblock` — unblocking
- `--filtering` — with filtering

```
chimera dns provider-edit my Quad9 9.9.9.9 149.112.112.112
```

#### `chimera dns provider-hide <id> [on|off]`

Hide a built-in DNS provider from the list or bring it back. Level: changes the app.

- `id` — built-in provider id
- `hidden` — true to hide, false to bring back

```
chimera dns provider-hide google
chimera dns provider-hide google false
```

#### `chimera dns trial <adapter> <provider> [--seconds <seconds>]`

Set DNS with an automatic rollback: if you do not confirm within --seconds seconds, the previous one comes back. Level: changes the system.

- `adapter` — adapter number from `chimera dns state`
- `provider` — provider id
- `--seconds` — seconds to confirm (5–120)

```
chimera dns trial 12 cloudflare
chimera dns trial 12 cloudflare --seconds 30
```

#### `chimera dns trial-confirm [adapter]`

Keep the new DNS after `dns trial`; without an adapter, all pending ones. Level: changes the app.

- `adapter` — adapter number; without it, all of them

```
chimera dns trial-confirm 12
```

#### `chimera dns trial-revert [adapter]`

Bring the previous DNS back right away, without waiting for the timer. Level: changes the system.

- `adapter` — adapter number; without it, all of them

```
chimera dns trial-revert 12
```

#### `chimera dns record-start`

Start recording a site's domains: it remembers the names in the Windows DNS cache (the cache is flushed if you have administrator rights). Level: changes the app.

```
chimera dns record-start
```

#### `chimera dns record-stop`

Finish recording: the domains that appeared since the start, grouped by main domain; trackers are marked. Open the site you need between start and stop. Level: changes the app.

```
chimera dns record-start
chimera dns record-stop --json
```

### panic

Turn everything off at once: bypass, proxy, Telegram, hosts, DNS, service.

#### `chimera panic`

Turn everything off at once: bypass, proxy, Telegram proxy, service, hosts substitution; put DNS back on the adapters where Chimera set it. The steps are independent, so one failing does not stop the others. Only when the user asks. Level: changes the system.

```
chimera panic
```

### doctor

Diagnostics: why the bypass may not work.

#### `chimera doctor [--report]`

Diagnostics: rights, WinDivert driver, ports, foreign processes, system proxy. --report gives Markdown for an issue (proxy links and secrets are hidden). Changes nothing. Level: read-only.

- `--report` — report in Markdown

```
chimera doctor
chimera doctor --report
chimera doctor --json
```

### lists

Domain lists.

#### `chimera lists show [name]`

Lists with domain counts and connections; with a name, the contents of that list. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `name` — list; without it, all of them

```
chimera lists show
chimera lists show youtube
```

#### `chimera lists save <name> [--file <file>]`

Write a whole list from a file (--file) or stdin. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

- `name` — list
- `--file` — list file; without it, stdin

```
chimera lists save youtube --file youtube.txt
```

#### `chimera lists create <name>`

Create an empty list. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

- `name` — Latin letters, digits, . - _

```
chimera lists create games
```

#### `chimera lists delete <name>`

Delete a list. Level: changes the app.

- `name` — str

```
chimera lists delete games
```

#### `chimera lists rename <old> <new>`

Rename a list together with the references to it. Level: changes the app.

- `old` — str
- `new` — str

```
chimera lists rename games play
```

#### `chimera lists add <name> <domains…>`

Add domains to a list (the list is created if it does not exist). Applied right away. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

- `name` — str
- `domains` — domains or subnets

```
chimera lists add youtube ytimg.com googlevideo.com
```

#### `chimera lists remove <name> <domains…>`

Remove domains from a list. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

- `name` — str
- `domains` — domains or subnets

```
chimera lists remove youtube ytimg.com
```

#### `chimera lists validate [name]`

Check a list file without changing anything: encoding, domain and subnet syntax, duplicates. Without a name, all lists. Errors mean exit code 1. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `name` — list; without it, all of them

```
chimera lists validate
chimera lists validate youtube --json
```

#### `chimera lists apply [name]`

Apply a list to the bypass, proxy and hosts now (without a name, all of them). Usually unnecessary: the running program picks up edits to lists/*.txt on disk by itself, and saving with `lists save` applies right away. Needs a running Chimera, with the window or in the tray. Level: changes the app.

- `name` — list; without it, all of them

```
chimera lists apply
chimera lists apply youtube
```

### check

Whether a site opens and whether it is blocked.

#### `chimera check site <domain> [--only <only>]`

Check one domain: whether it is reachable from this computer and whether it is in the block registry. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `domain` — domain or address
- `--only` — local or registry only

```
chimera check discord.com
chimera check site discord.com --only local
```

#### `chimera check list <list> [--only <only>]`

Check all the domains of a list (in parallel), like “Check list” in the window. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `list` — list name
- `--only` — local or registry only

```
chimera check list discord
```

#### `chimera check status`

State of the block registry service (version, update date). Level: read-only.

```
chimera check status
```

### logs

Last lines of the module logs.

#### `chimera logs <winws|proxy|tg> [--tail <tail>]`

Last lines of a module's log: winws, proxy or tg. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `module` — module
- `--tail` — how many last lines (40 by default)

```
chimera logs winws
chimera logs proxy --tail 100
```

### service

Windows background service.

#### `chimera service <install|uninstall|start|stop|status|run> [params…]`

Background service: install, uninstall, start, stop, status, run (like `main.py service`). Level: changes the system. Works without a running Chimera.

- `command` — action
- `params` — for example --dry-run

```
chimera service status
chimera service install --dry-run
```

### path

The chimera command in the user's PATH.

#### `chimera path show`

Whether the program folder is in the user's PATH. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

```
chimera path show
```

#### `chimera path add`

Add the program folder to the user's PATH (after that `chimera` works from any folder). Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

```
chimera path add
```

#### `chimera path remove`

Remove the program folder from the user's PATH. Level: changes the app. Works without a running Chimera.

```
chimera path remove
```

### docs

Documentation for this version: commands, folders and files, output format.

#### `chimera docs [commands|layout|output]`

Documentation for this version of the program. Topics: commands, layout (folders and files), output (exit codes and the --json format). Without a topic, the table of contents; with --json, everything in machine-readable form. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

- `topic` — topic

```
chimera docs
chimera docs layout
chimera docs --json
```

### agent-info

Summary for agents: versions, commands with levels, paths (`--json`).

#### `chimera agent-info`

Summary for agents: program and protocol version, compatible skill version, commands with levels, data paths. Use --json for machine parsing. Level: read-only. Works without a running Chimera.

```
chimera agent-info --json
```

### trial

Try settings with checks and automatic rollback..

#### `chimera trial state`

Current trial, check results and last completed trial. Original state and secrets are not returned. Level: read-only.

```
chimera trial state --json
```

#### `chimera trial start <strategy|hosts|tun> <target> [--seconds <seconds>] [--domains <domains>]`

Try a strategy, the hosts switch or a TUN mode. Checks control sites; restores the original state on failure or without confirmation. One trial at a time; other changes are blocked until it finishes. Level: changes the system.

- `kind` — strategy, hosts or tun
- `target` — strategy ID, on/off for hosts, or split/tun
- `--seconds` — confirmation window: 15–300 seconds
- `--domains` — comma-separated control domains (up to 6); defaults to example.com,cloudflare.com

```
chimera trial start strategy general --seconds 60 --domains example.com,discord.com
chimera trial start hosts on
chimera trial start tun tun
```

#### `chimera trial confirm <id>`

Keep settings after successful checks. Requires the current trial ID; expired trials cannot be confirmed. Level: changes the app.

- `id` — current trial ID from trial state

```
chimera trial confirm 0123456789abcdef
```

#### `chimera trial revert <id>`

Restore original settings and module runtime state. On error, keeps the data for another rollback attempt. Level: changes the system.

- `id` — current trial ID from trial state

```
chimera trial revert 0123456789abcdef
```

### explain

Why an address matches a route.

#### `chimera explain <domain> [--app <app>]`

Explain rules for a domain or IP: lists, DPI, PAC/TUN, application and hosts entries. Reads local settings without DNS requests or changes. Level: read-only.

- `domain` — domain, IP or HTTP(S) URL without credentials
- `--app` — process name, for example Discord.exe; for selective TUN

```
chimera explain youtube.com
chimera explain 192.168.1.1 --app chrome.exe
chimera explain discord.com --app Discord.exe --json
```

## Files

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `config.json` | can be edited: Program settings. Change them with `chimera config set` (some keys only by editing the file). |
| `lists/*.txt` | can be edited: Domain and subnet lists, one entry per line, # starts a comment. Commands `chimera lists …`. The running program picks up direct edits to the file by itself within a couple of seconds (create, change, delete); check a file with `chimera lists validate`. |
| `strategies/*.txt` | generated, do not edit: winws2 strategies, ported from Flowseal (tools/port_flowseal.py). Do not edit. |
| `strategies/hostlists/list-general-user.txt` | generated, do not edit: Built from the lists selected for the bypass. Do not edit. |
| `strategies/hostlists/ipset-user.txt` | generated, do not edit: Subnets from the selected lists. Do not edit. |
| `strategies/hostlists/list-exclude-user.txt` | can be edited: Exclusion domains for the bypass. Edit only when the user asks. |
| `strategies/hostlists/ipset-exclude-user.txt` | can be edited: Exclusion subnets for the bypass. Edit only when the user asks. |
| `strategies/hostlists/ipset-all.txt` | can be edited: The common subnet list (ipset mode). Changed by `chimera winws ipset …` commands. |
| `data/winws.json` | internal state: Last strategy, selected lists, bypass autostart. Change with `chimera winws …` commands. |
| `data/proxy.json` | secret: Proxy link (credentials), mode, lists, apps. Do not read or show. |
| `data/tgproxy.json` | secret: Port, secret and parameters of the Telegram proxy. Do not read or show. |
| `data/hosts.json` | internal state: Bindings of lists to hosts providers, background options. `chimera hosts …` commands. |
| `data/dns_providers.user.json` | internal state: DNS providers added by the user. `chimera dns provider-…` commands. |
| `data/singbox-config.json` | generated, do not edit: sing-box config. Rebuilt by the program. |
| `data/singbox-domains.json` | generated, do not edit: Domains of the lists selected for the proxy (a sing-box rule file). Rebuilt. |
| `data/singbox-ips.json` | generated, do not edit: Subnets of the lists selected for the proxy. Rebuilt. |
| `data/proxy.pac` | generated, do not edit: The PAC file of the pac mode. Rebuilt. |
| `data/logs/*.log` | log, read only: Module logs (winws, proxy, tgproxy, hosts, service, update). Read them with `chimera logs <module>`. |
| `data/changes.log` | log, read only: Change log: time, source (`cli` for a command, `file` for a list edit on disk), command, result (`ok` or `error`). |
| `data/control.json` | secret: Port and token of the control channel. An agent does not need to read it; do not show it. |
| `data/backups/` | secret: Local snapshots before import/restoration (last 10). May contain secrets; do not publish. List and restore with chimera config backups / restore-preview / restore. |
| `data/trial.json` | internal state: Original state of an unfinished trial. Do not edit; chimera trial state / confirm / revert. |
| `bin/` | external, do not edit: Binaries (sing-box, winws2). Do not edit. |
| `upstream/` | external, do not edit: External projects (submodules). Do not edit. |
